- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent history shows sharp spikes followed by rapid declines, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast rise after spike by 5–10% below peak.  
- If true outcome deviates significantly from forecast in early days (1–3), adjust forecast downward if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for next period if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating highs/lows), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
